subject: Computer independent data description
notes: Rule: 'The non-combining character and the following combining characters of a composite sequence defined in ISO/IEC 10646 are each treated as a single character position.' (cite.py --check 8.5.1.4 -> OK §8.5.1.4 1)). The typed-native substrate stores alphanumeric and national text as .NET UTF-16 code units, one char per character position (D-N1; CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-188), with no grapheme/StringInfo/normalization anywhere on the character-position path (searched src for StringInfo/TextElement/EnumerateRunes/Normalize: only the ISO 14651 collation engine and CLDR builder walk codepoints, which is the STANDARD-COMPARE algorithm, not character-position processing). PROBE (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023, out/probe/cidd/p1.cob): N"e"+U+0301 -> FUNCTION LENGTH = 2; PIC N(3) VALUE that literal: (1:1) = N"e", (2:1) = NX"0301"; INSPECT TALLYING FOR CHARACTERS BEFORE N" " = 02. All as the rule requires (base and mark each one position). No spec-derived golden pins a combining sequence (grep of tests/conformance for 0301/combining: none) -> test-ref empty. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the ISO/IEC 10646 / UTF-16 national facility enters with ISO 1989:2002; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to 8.5.1.4; X3.23-1985 has no ISO/IEC 10646 coded character set, so the rule is vacuous at 85)
